report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of 3 of daedalus/council/bus.py. All docstring claims are verifiable within this chunk: KEPT. No broken claims, checks that cannot fail, inverted rules, or format-pinning issues found.

handoff.purpose: Contains public append APIs (append_round, append_turn, append_roster), reading functions (load_transcript, transcript_head, read_anchor), and tamper verification (verify_chain).

symbols.name: append_round
symbols.note: Chains a whole round. Normalizes turns, applies secret-floor rules, sorts by actor and canonical body, then chains records.

symbols.name: append_turn
symbols.note: Convenience over append_round for a single turn.

symbols.name: append_roster
symbols.note: Chains a roster accounting record. Validates participants, computes counts and degraded flag, applies roster scanning rules.

symbols.name: load_transcript
symbols.note: Reads all records from store path, skipping torn lines and empty lines.

symbols.name: read_anchor
symbols.note: Reads the anchor file and returns its content as a dict.

symbols.name: verify_chain
symbols.note: Walks the chain and reports failures. Checks body_sha, entry_sha, prev linkage, and optionally tail truncation via anchor.

claims.text: Turns are normalised, secret-floored, then sorted by actor id and chained with ``seq`` assigned here -- so reversed completion order yields a byte-identical chain head.
claims.why: Code normalizes each turn via _normalize_turn (line 596), applies secret-floor via _scan_turn (line 597), and sorts by (actor, role, status, canonical_body_json) (line 615). Sorting ensures deterministic order.

claims.text: Exactly one turn per actor per round is allowed: a duplicate is a caller bug that would double a voice, and a missing participant must be recorded as an ``unavailable`` turn rather than skipped.
claims.why: Code checks for duplicates (lines 606-610) and raises ValueError if any actor appears more than once (excluding 'council.redacted.redacted').

claims.text: a round with no turns is not a round: every requested participant produces exactly one chained turn
claims.why: Line 593-595 raises ValueError if turns is empty.

claims.text: REFUSE. The offending bytes never reach the file -- not in the turn, nor in the receipt.
claims.why: If _scan_turn returns a rule, the receipt is generated via _refusal_receipt and replaces the original turn (lines 599-603). The original turn is not appended.

claims.text: Chain a single turn (a one-participant round). Convenience over :func:`append_round`; prefer the round form so ordering stays deterministic.
claims.why: append_turn calls append_round with a single-turn list and returns the first element (line 623). Determinism is inherited from append_round.

claims.text: Chain the roster accounting: requested / seated / responded / unavailable with machine reasons, plus the DISTINCT INDEPENDENCE CLASS count and a ``degraded`` flag whenever fewer participants responded than were requested.
claims.why: Code computes requested, seated, responded, unavailable, distinct_classes, duplicate_classes, and degraded (lines 663-671). These are included in the record (lines 673-681).

claims.text: Counts are DERIVED here, never accepted from the caller: "3 of 4" and "2 of 2" must not be able to render as the same string, and a consumer that shows the participant count instead of the distinct-class count is showing a council of clones as a council.
claims.why: Counts are computed from the normalized participants (lines 663-671) and stored as integers, not strings. The caller's input is not used for these counts.
Line 641 raises ValueError if phase not in ('open', 'close').
Line 647 checks actor against _ACTOR_RE regex, which presumably enforces the pattern.

claims.text: outcome must be one of PARTICIPANT_OUTCOMES
claims.why: Line 650-652 raises ValueError if outcome not in PARTICIPANT_OUTCOMES.

claims.text: Duplicate weights are detected over everyone SEATED ... the distinct-class count is over those who actually RESPONDED
claims.why: Lines 658-660: seated_classes includes those with outcome in ('seated','responded','refused'); heard_classes includes only 'responded'. Lines 663-664 compute duplicates from seated_classes, distinct_classes from heard_classes.

claims.text: Read all records, skipping a torn tail line (never fatal). Missing is [].
claims.why: Code returns [] if store_path does not exist (line 686). It iterates over lines, skips empty lines, and catches json.JSONDecodeError to skip unparseable lines (lines 690-694).

claims.text: ``(record_count, head_entry_sha)`` -- the tail anchor, recomputed from the file. Compare against :func:`read_anchor` to catch a truncation.
claims.why: transcript_head calls load_transcript and returns (len(records), records[-1].get('entry_sha') if records else None) (lines 698-700).

claims.text: Walk the chain; return ``(ok, failures)`` where every failure NAMES the 1-indexed line and what mismatched. Never a bare False.
claims.why: Function returns tuple (bool, list[str]) (line 705). Failures are strings that name the line number and issue (e.g., lines 724, 727, 731, 733, 737, 741, 744).

claims.text: Three independent checks per line: * ``body_sha`` recomputed over the canonical body -- catches a content edit; * ``entry_sha`` recomputed over ``(prev, stored body_sha, ts)`` -- catches a back-dated ts or a rewritten link where body_sha WAS updated; * ``prev`` equals the previous line's ``entry_sha`` -- catches a deleted or reordered line
claims.why: Lines 723-725 check body_sha; lines 726-728 check entry_sha; lines 729-732 check prev linkage.

claims.text: TAIL truncation is the one deletion a per-line walk cannot catch ... the persisted anchor is consulted by default and a shortfall in count or head is NAMED. Explicit ``expected_count`` / ``expected_head`` override it; ``use_anchor=False`` verifies linkage only.
claims.why: Lines 710-713: if use_anchor and no explicit expected values, anchor is read. Lines 737-739 check n_records vs expected_count; lines 741-743 check prev_entry_sha vs expected_head.

observations.what: append_round sorts by canonical_body_json as final tiebreak, ensuring deterministic order even for anonymised receipts with same actor/role/status.
append_roster's duplicate detection uses seated_classes (includes 'refused') but distinct_classes uses heard_classes (only 'responded'). This matches docstring.
verify_chain continues to next line even if JSON parsing fails, leaving prev_entry_sha unchanged so subsequent lines also flag broken linkage.
If store_path does not exist, verify_chain returns failures only if expected_count or expected_head is provided; otherwise returns (True, []) (no failures).
